feature: Command R opens a clip's speed
summary: Command R, Premiere's Speed/Duration key, opens the Speed list in the panel for the picked piece, bringing the panel back and opening the Time section if either was put away. Clip ▸ Change Speed… carries the key so it can be learned from the menu.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a recording and cut it at two seconds: press B and click the clip there, or put the playhead there and press Command K.
Click the second piece on the timeline.
Pick 2x from the list that dropped open.
Fold the Time section by its header, then press Command R again.
Open Clip in the menu bar and find Change Speed… with Command R beside it.
Make a new empty video and press Command R.

evaluate: Does the Speed list dropping open under the panel's Speed row feel like Premiere's Speed/Duration, or do you want a box of its own on the canvas?
With nothing clicked, Command R opens the speed of the piece under the playhead and picks it. Is that what you expect?
Is Change Speed… above the Speed submenu in the Clip menu the right way to show the key, or is two speed rows one too many?
On a held frame Command R opens its Hold list instead. Is that the right answer for a frame with no speed?
rough: The pictures show the Speed dropdown with its open edge but not the list itself: a walk never puts a real menu on screen, so the list a person sees when it drops open was not photographed. The panel's own click opens the same menu the same way.
No mock covers a key for speed; the list it opens is the panel's own Speed dropdown, unchanged.
